add.issue.name: greeter: per-user avatar on the login screen

edit.description.md:
Show a chosen image beside the username on the greetd login screen.

The greeter already stages wallpaper and palette snapshots into
/etc/aphotic/greeter for the greeter user to read. An avatar is the same
shape of problem, so reuse that path rather than inventing a second one.

Constraints that shape the design:

- The greeter runs as the greeter system user before anyone has
  authenticated, so it has no read access to the real user's home
  directory. The image has to be staged into a root-owned snapshot dir.
- Sync happens through `aphotic greeter sync` in
  commands/cmd_greeter.sh.
- Files have to end up world readable. _aphotic_greeter_write stages
  through mktemp and a plain cp, which carries 0600 across, so uid 947
  cannot read the result. Fix that in the same change.
- The greeter does not know who is typing until the name is submitted, so
  the snapshot needs a name to avatar mapping. Decide where that lives: a
  manifest json beside the snapshot, one file per login name, or a single
  avatar for every user.
- Keep the degraded state quiet. No avatar means the current layout with no
  image, and no error text.

Open question: per user avatars, or one avatar for the whole machine.

Done when a user can set an avatar, it survives a reboot, it appears for
that user at the login screen, and a missing or unreadable avatar leaves
the current layout untouched.

add.issue.name: settings: profile picture in the settings menu

edit.description.md:
Put a profile picture in the settings menu.

The settings surface carries no user identity at all right now, so this is
a new element rather than a change to an existing one.

Constraints:

- Local first. No cloud, and no new external dependency. The image lives
  under the user's own config directory.
- Settings is Quickshell QML. Use the existing file dialog helper and load
  the result with a file URL.
- The shell already has a cache-busting pattern in the live Wallpapers.qml
  for an image that gets overwritten in place. Follow it, or a re-picked
  avatar shows the old one.
- Persist the choice through the existing settings service and add the key
  to the same schema, so it round-trips through the normal config sync.
- Clearing the avatar has to return the header to its current layout
  without leaving a gap.

Open question: header only, or the panel as well.

Done when an avatar can be picked and cleared, it survives a reboot, and a
missing or unreadable image leaves the settings menu as it looks now.

add.issue.name: /mnt/windows never mounts when the NVMe enumerates after the fstab generator

edit.description.md:
## Symptom

`/mnt/windows` is empty on boot, so `llama-swap` crash-loops (restart counter 114 on 2026-09-27) and the homelab config promotion never runs.

## Not an unmount

The journal shows four unmounts on 2026-09-27 (12:19, 12:54, 13:02, 13:12) and they are all ordinary shutdowns. Each is preceded by `user@1000.service: Deactivated successfully` and `Reached target Exit the Session`; the box was rebooting every 7 to 10 minutes in that window. The volume mounted correctly on every one of those boots.

## Actual cause

A boot-order race in `systemd-fstab-generator`. At 13:13:16 it emitted a zero-length unit, which systemd reads as masked:

```
 393  /run/systemd/generator/boot.mount
 345  /run/systemd/generator/mnt-nfs.mount
   0  /run/systemd/generator/mnt-windows.mount   <- empty, i.e. masked
 362  /run/systemd/generator/-.mount
```

The fstab source is `UUID=2EA4E311A4E2D9FB` (`/dev/nvme0n1p2`, label `Data`, holding `E:\llama-swap`). When `/dev/disk/by-uuid` is not yet populated when the generator runs, the entry resolves to nothing and the unit comes out empty. Nothing pulls it into `local-fs.target.wants`, `nofail` keeps the failure silent, and the entry's own `x-systemd.device-timeout=10` cannot help because there is no unit for the device dependency to live in.

Running the same generator by hand with the device present produces a valid 329-byte unit, so the fstab options themselves are fine:

```
What=/dev/disk/by-uuid/2EA4E311A4E2D9FB
Where=/mnt/windows
Type=ntfs3
Options=rw,uid=1000,gid=1000,windows_names,nofail
```

This will recur on any boot where that NVMe enumerates after the generator.

## Blast radius

Beyond llama-swap, both of these carry `RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/windows` and have been down for the same reason:

- `lsw-apply.service` (every 2 min) -- the repo's desired llama-swap config is not being promoted to the shared live file on any schedule
- `lab-sync.service` (every 5 min)

So the shared live config is currently unmaintained. Do not repoint the llama-swap unit at `homelab/reference/llama-swap/config.yaml` as a workaround: the live file is deliberately shared with the Windows boot and `lsw-apply` is what keeps the two in step.

## Fix chosen

Replace the fstab automount with a static `/etc/systemd/system/mnt-windows.mount` that holds the mount job until the partition appears. `/etc/systemd/system` takes precedence over `/run/systemd/generator`, and the device dependency can be formed there, so the race is gone rather than narrowed. Same filesystem, driver, options and ownership as the fstab entry, keeping `nofail` and `x-systemd.device-timeout=10` so an absent disk still lets boot proceed.

Staged and ready to run, needs root:

- `/tmp/opencode/mnt-windows-fix/mnt-windows.mount`
- `/tmp/opencode/mnt-windows-fix/install.sh` (idempotent, backs up fstab, refuses to force a mount the kernel rejects)

```
sudo bash /tmp/opencode/mnt-windows-fix/install.sh
```

Note on mechanism: a `RUN+="/usr/bin/mount"` udev rule was considered and not used. udev runs `RUN` in a restricted context where `mount` is unreliable, and it does not give the boot a place to wait. The static mount unit is the systemd-native way to get mount-on-device-appearance.

## Verification done and not done

- Done: generator run by hand produces a valid unit; `systemd-analyze verify` accepts the staged unit; journal evidence for every unmount captured; `lsw-apply` and `lab-sync` failures confirmed.
- Not done: the mount itself is unverified. No sudo on this session, so the install has not been run and no reboot has been exercised.

add.issue.name: BAR-04: DockWorkspaces motion and colour tokens (lands on dock and minimal)

edit.description.md:
Shared by the dock and the minimal style, and by nothing else. Consumers are exactly `DockBar.qml:241` and `MinimalBar.qml:62`, so one change lands on both and there is no third style to regress.

Work:

- `occupiedColour` at `DockWorkspaces.qml:20` is `m3onSurfaceVariant`. The full bar's occupied workspace pill is `Colours.layer(Colours.palette.m3surfaceContainerHigh, 2)`. Align it. Check legibility on light and dark themes, since this is a real colour change and not a token rename.
- `dotSize: 6` / `activeDotSize: 14` at `:25-26` are pixel constants. Tokenise. Note `activeDotSize` is coupled to the HoverPill diameter at `:62`, so change both in the same pass or the active dot stops sitting centred in the pill.
- Bare `Anim {}` on `Layout.preferredWidth`/`Height` at `:90,94`. Make the type explicit; a bare `Anim` resolves to `DefaultSpatial` (500ms, `components/Anim.qml:22`).

Deliberately NOT in scope: the dock's magnification, which the code already documents as mutually exclusive with a gliding hover highlight (`DockBar.qml:197-202`).

Risk: low. Nothing in modules/bar does arithmetic on `Tokens.rounding`, and no layout depends on the dot's radius.

Verify with the windowless headless probe per docs/playbooks/qml-verification.md. The colour change needs the operator's eye; the probe only proves it does not throw.

add.issue.name: BAR-05: Taskbar style joins the full bar's hover and colour roles

edit.description.md:
The largest real gap of the four. Two pieces of work.

## 1. Focused task item colour

`TaskbarBar.qml:208` uses `m3secondaryContainer` for a focused item and `m3surfaceContainerHigh` for unfocused. The full bar puts active/primary state on `m3primary` (workspace active pill, agent badge). This is the one visibly breaking colour in the whole pass and the biggest single visual change in the plan. Confirm it is wanted before starting.

The count badge at `:222-232` already uses `m3primary` + `Colours.contrastOn`, which matches `AgentIndicator`'s badge. Leave it.

## 2. Adopt the shared HoverPill

`TaskbarBar.qml` never instantiates `HoverPill`; task items use `StateLayer` (`:237-262`). `HoverPill` is in scope via `import "components"` at `:3` but unused.

Nothing about it is numerically specific to the full bar. The blockers are structural, and all three are known:

1. `HoverPill` positions itself from `container.x/.y` and reads `hoveredEntry.x/.width` directly, so both must be direct siblings inside a plain `Item`. The taskbar's `Repeater` (`:167-177`) is a direct child of `RowLayout` (`:138`), so it needs a plain-`Item` wrapper, exactly the way `DockBar.qml:172-230` already does this.
2. `HoverPill` has non-zero implicit size, so left directly in a `RowLayout` it takes a layout slot and shifts every entry. The wrapper from (1) is what prevents that.
3. Z-order is declaration order only, there is no `z`, so it must be declared before the icon row.

Orientation is hardwired to `Settings.barHorizontal`, which the taskbar already honours. Diameter caps at `Settings.barInnerWidth`, which matches the taskbar's square entry boxes.

Keep `radius: 0` on the strip itself (`:135`): the contract's pill radius governs entries, not the whole bar, and the taskbar is deliberately full-bleed.

Reference implementation to copy: `StatusIcons.qml`, which is already instantiated by this style and conforms.

Verify with the windowless headless probe. Both changes are visual and need the operator's eye.

add.issue.name: BAR-06: Capsule popout depth, radius behaviour and motion

edit.description.md:
The capsule is the most conformant of the four already. Most of its apparent divergence is deliberate. Three open questions, then a small tidy-up.

## Deliberate, do not change

- Rotated rounded-square workspace cells (`CapsuleWorkspaces.qml:67-71`). The comment gives the reason: a rotated square reads as a shape change without costing a path rebuild.
- `rounding.small` transport end-caps (`CapsuleTransport.qml:23`). Media-control specific.
- `rounding.extraLarge` (28) on the pill at `CapsuleBar.qml:117,263`. At the default thickness of 56 this is exactly half, so QML's clamp already renders it as a full pill, identical to `rounding.full`.
- `CapsuleArtwork.qml:96` and `CapsuleMediaSurface.qml:120` use token-resolved `Anim` types consistent with the rest. Leave.

## Open question 1: the radius in the swollen state

`rowThickness = max(Settings.barInnerWidth, rowCross) + padding.extraSmall * 2` (`CapsuleBar.qml:38`). The growth with `rowCross` is deliberate. Past 56 the thickness exceeds 56, at which point 28 is no longer half the height and the capsule becomes a rounded rectangle while every other style stays a pill. That behaviour difference, not the value, is the divergence. Should the capsule stay a rounded rectangle when it swells, or go fully pill?

## Open question 2: popout shadow mechanism

`popoutSurface` (`:253-284`) uses `ShapeShadow` (`:266-272`). The full bar's flyout uses `Elevation { level: 2 }`. These are different mechanisms and both are current: `ShapeShadow` is the newer of the two (`97a97d6`, 2026-09-10) and exists to avoid a `layer`+`MultiEffect` on always-visible chrome, while `Elevation` replaced the old layer shadow in popouts and live-tracks its target. The capsule's surface is width/height-animated, which is the case `Elevation` handles and `ShapeShadow` does not. Swapping is a mechanism change and wants a visual check, not a mechanical one.

Note: if `BAR-03` (popouts on every bar style) lands first, this question largely answers itself, because the capsule would route through the shared wrapper.

`ConcaveCorner` does not apply here. The capsule's popout is a flush sibling extending the pill, not a separate surface meeting the bar edge, so there is no bar-side corner to fillet.

## Open question 3: popout reach motion

`:239,245` animate the reach on `Anim.DefaultSpatial` (500ms) where the contract's flyout motion is `Anim.FastSpatial` (350ms). A deliberate feel change rather than a fix.

## Tidy-up

`CapsuleMediaChip.qml:33-34` uses `m3secondaryContainer` when active. Check against the colour-role rule; likely a `m3primary` alignment like BAR-05's taskbar change.

Verify with the windowless headless probe. Every item here is visual.

add.issue.name: BAR-07: Record the deliberate bar-style divergences so they stop reading as bugs

edit.description.md:
A read-only pass over the four non-full bar styles found a long list of apparent divergences from the full bar's design language. Most turned out to be deliberate, documented decisions, and two were simply wrong. Both facts are worth keeping in the repo so a later pass does not "fix" them.

## Wrong claims, corrected

- `Anim.StandardSmall` is not a divergence. The full bar uses it too (`Workspaces.qml:288`, `SpecialWorkspaces.qml:134,139`). `Tokens.anim.*` are duration and easing tokens that every `Anim` type resolves to, not the types themselves. Conflating the two is what made this look like drift.
- `ShapeShadow` is not legacy superseded by `Elevation`. It is newer (`97a97d6`, 2026-09-10). `Elevation` replaced the old `layer` shadow in popouts. Both are current and they are different mechanisms.

## Deliberate, already documented in the code, needs no change

- Dock: no `HoverPill` while magnification is on. `DockBar.qml:197-202` states a gliding highlight under swelling icons reads as two effects fighting, and the guard is real (`:205`, `:226`).
- Dock: no popout system. Tracked by `BAR-03`, not a styling gap.
- Minimal: border-only strip with an `m3primary` border and no fill. `MinimalBar.qml:37-45` gives the reasoning, accent is reserved for active state and never a whole background.
- Minimal: bare icons with no pill grouping. Sparseness is the style.
- Taskbar: `radius: 0` full-bleed strip. The pill radius governs entries, not the whole bar.
- Capsule: rotated rounded-square workspace cells, `rounding.small` transport end-caps. Both commented in place.

## Also worth knowing

`StatusIcons.qml` is instantiated by all five styles including the full bar, and it already conforms to the target design language. It is the reference implementation to copy from. Changes to it land everywhere at once, so it should be treated as load-bearing and not redesigned as part of the other-style work.

`DockWorkspaces.qml` has exactly two consumers, `DockBar.qml:241` and `MinimalBar.qml:62`.

Suggested outcome: fold these notes into the existing comments where they are already partly there, and correct the two wrong claims anywhere they have been repeated. No behaviour change.

add.issue.comment.md:
Reviewed the four non-full bar styles on `feature/ui-refresh-p3-bar`, every claim verified against source. Not claiming this work, flagging it so it folds in rather than running parallel. Full notes in `docs/design/p3c-plan.md` in that worktree.

## What the full bar's cohesion actually is

Not a per-widget look. `Bar.qml` is byte-identical between `main` and this branch, so the refresh landed almost entirely outside it: four shared primitives (`HoverPill`, `Elevation`, `ConcaveCorner`, `SurfaceReveal`), colour by role, and every animation on an explicit `Anim` type plus `Tokens.anim.*`. `StatusIcons.qml` is the reference implementation of the target state and all five styles already instantiate it.

## Most apparent divergence is deliberate and should stay

- Dock: no `HoverPill` while magnification is on. `DockBar.qml:197-202` calls magnification and a gliding highlight two effects fighting, and the guard is real (`:205`, `:226`).
- Minimal: border-only strip, no fill. `MinimalBar.qml:37-45`, accent is reserved for active state and never a whole background.
- Taskbar: `radius: 0` full-bleed. The pill radius governs entries, not the strip.
- Capsule: rotated rounded-square workspace cells (`CapsuleWorkspaces.qml:67-71`), `rounding.small` transport end-caps. Both commented in place.

## Two claims to correct before acting

- `Anim.StandardSmall` is not drift. The full bar uses it too (`Workspaces.qml:288`, `SpecialWorkspaces.qml:134,139`). `Tokens.anim.*` are duration and easing tokens that every `Anim` type resolves to, not the types themselves.
- `ShapeShadow` is not legacy superseded by `Elevation`. It is newer (`97a97d6`, 2026-09-10) and avoids a `layer`+`MultiEffect` on always-visible chrome. `Elevation` replaced the old layer shadow in popouts. Different mechanisms, both current.

## Concrete work, smallest first

1. `DockWorkspaces.qml`: occupied colour at `:20` is `m3onSurfaceVariant` where full bar uses `Colours.layer(m3surfaceContainerHigh, 2)`; `dotSize`/`activeDotSize` at `:25-26` are pixel constants coupled to the HoverPill diameter at `:62`; bare `Anim {}` at `:90,94`. Exactly two consumers, `DockBar.qml:241` and `MinimalBar.qml:62`, so one change lands on both.
2. Taskbar: focused item is `m3secondaryContainer` at `:208` where active state is `m3primary` elsewhere, and no `HoverPill` at all. Adoption is structural, not numeric. The `Repeater` (`:167-177`) is a direct `RowLayout` child (`:138`) and needs a plain-`Item` wrapper the way `DockBar.qml:172-230` does: `HoverPill` has non-zero implicit size and would take a layout slot, and its z-order is declaration order only.
3. Dock after that: only `DockAppIcon`'s hardcoded 5x5 running dot (`:60-69`).
4. Capsule: `popoutSurface` uses `ShapeShadow` (`:266-272`) on a width/height-animated surface, the case `Elevation` handles by live-tracking. `ConcaveCorner` does not apply, the popout is a flush sibling extending the pill, not a surface meeting the bar edge. Also `rowThickness` (`:38`) grows with `rowCross`, so past 56 the `extraLarge` radius of 28 stops being half the height and the capsule becomes a rounded rectangle while other styles stay pills. Design call.

No layout depends on entry radius. Nothing in modules/bar does arithmetic on `Tokens.rounding`, and QML clamps radius to half the minor dimension.

## Conflict to resolve first

This ticket asks for the Signal direction, which includes a quiet rest state with muted icons and no filled pills. Aligning the four styles to the full bar's current properties pulls the opposite way, since full bar entries are `m3surfaceContainerHigh` filled pills. Both cannot hold. The hover-pill and pill-fill items invert depending on the answer, so decide this before per-style work starts.

`BAR-03` (popouts on every bar style) is adjacent. If it lands first, dock and capsule pick up the shared popout chrome and the capsule `ShapeShadow` question largely answers itself.

add.issue.comment.md:
Fixed on this host. The installer was run as root and the mount is up.

**Diagnosis held.** `systemd-fstab-generator` had emitted a zero-length `/run/systemd/generator/mnt-windows.mount`, which systemd reads as masked. The fstab source is a `UUID=` that had not resolved into `/dev/disk/by-uuid` when the generator ran, so the entry produced no unit, nothing pulled it into `local-fs.target.wants`, and `nofail` kept it silent.

**What was installed.** `/etc/systemd/system/mnt-windows.mount`, a static unit that takes precedence over the fstab generator and holds the mount job on the device until the partition appears:

```
BindsTo=dev-disk-by\x2duuid-2EA4E311A4E2D9FB.device
After=dev-disk-by\x2duuid-2EA4E311A4E2D9FB.device
Before=local-fs.target
...
Options=rw,uid=1000,gid=1000,windows_names,nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=10
```

The fstab line is commented out (line 12) so there is one source of truth, and `/etc/fstab.bak-20260927T133912` is the backup.

**Result.** `/mnt/windows` mounted from `/dev/nvme0n1p2` with the intended options, unit `enabled` and `active`, `llama-swap` serving on 9090. `lsw-apply` and `lab-sync` recovered with it, since both carry `RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/windows`.

**Mechanism note.** The original plan was a udev rule. It was implemented as a static mount unit instead: udev runs `RUN` in a restricted context where `mount` is unreliable, and a `RUN+=` rule gives the boot nowhere to wait. `BindsTo` on the device is what actually closes the race. A udev trigger can be added on top if wanted, but it is not what fixed this.

**Two things still open, for the operator:**

1. The fix has not been exercised across a reboot. It is verified for this boot only. A reboot on a cold-boot path is the real test.
2. Decide whether the static unit permanently replaces the fstab entry. It currently does, because `/etc/systemd/system` outranks the generator and the fstab line is commented.

Reproduce the original condition by clearing the generated unit and watching it come back empty: `sudo rm -f /run/systemd/generator/mnt-windows.mount && sudo systemctl daemon-reexec`.

add.issue.comment.md:
Operator answered the conflict I raised here: the target is a shared **flow**, not the full bar copied onto the other four. Each style keeps its own shape, character and layout; what unifies them is the rhythm of movement and feedback, so the shell reads as one design instead of five unmatched bars.

That reframes the central question rather than closing it, and it is now recorded as such in `docs/design/p3c-plan.md` in the `aphotic-ui-p3` worktree.

## The question that now gates the work

If surface treatment stays per style, then which properties carry the cohesion? Four candidates, and they conflict with each other:

- **(a) Motion discipline only.** Every animation on an explicit `Anim` type over `Tokens.anim.*`, so all five styles move on the same rhythm. Touches no colour, no radius, no layout, and no deliberate divergence. Compatible with every style as it stands.
- **(b) Shared `HoverPill` hover.** Collides with the dock, which documents magnification and a gliding highlight as mutually exclusive (`DockBar.qml:197-202`).
- **(c) Colour roles and `m3surfaceContainerHigh` entry fills.** Collides with the minimal style's border-only design, and with the no-filled-pills direction in this ticket.
- **(d) `Elevation` on every flyout.** Collides with the capsule's `ShapeShadow`, which is the newer and cheaper mechanism for always-visible chrome.

Which are in, and which are explicitly out. (a) is the one that can be done without undoing anyone's deliberate decision, which is why it is worth naming first.

## Also open, lower stakes

- Does cohesive reach thickness. This ticket asks for slimmer bars; one thickness across all five styles or per-style is undecided.
- Capsule swollen state: `rowThickness` (`CapsuleBar.qml:38`) grows with content, so past 56px the `rounding.extraLarge` of 28 stops being half the height and the capsule renders as a rounded rectangle while the other four stay pills. Accept it, or go `rounding.full`.
- Taskbar focused item at `TaskbarBar.qml:208` uses `m3secondaryContainer` where active state is `m3primary` elsewhere. Only matters if (c) is in.
- `BAR-03` would hand dock and capsule the shared popout wrapper and largely answer the capsule depth question. Worth settling the sequencing before the capsule work starts.

This session is not taking the ticket. Full read-only review, verified against source, is in the earlier comment and in `docs/design/p3c-plan.md`.

The FTN6AW1 adapters hand the writer finished v2 records, but agent_hook.py reads only Claude's v1 hook vocabulary, so every adapter record is dropped and OpenCode sessions never reach the graph, audit or agents tile.

Two pieces:

- agent_hook.py: accept records that already carry the v2 markers (v 2, sessionId, a contract event kind), stamp the clock, and write them through the same three sinks as mapped records.
- AgentProviders: sum usage records off the event stream for harnesses the transcript scan cannot cover (OpenCode has no transcript to scan), so today's tokens show for them without double counting the scans it does cover.

Done when an OpenCode session shows the same fields in the graph, audit and agents tile as a Claude session.
